If sentiment is >0.5 in the last 3 days and forecast is trending down, increase the forecast by 1–2% to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment is <0.5 and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.  
In early horizon (1–7 days), if sentiment is consistently positive, shift forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 3-day average.  
In mid horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing correction toward historical mean.  
In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is negative and forecast is above 65, reduce by 1–2% to prevent overextension.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.0 in last 2 days and forecast is below 60, increase by 1–2% to align with bullish momentum.
